messages:
ken: Heads-up — acme-prod-eu2 opened a support escalation: p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~110ms -> ~920ms since Thu ~22:00 UTC. They attached traces and say it hits 4/20 nodes in their Dedicated pool.

mike: Can you paste the trace snippet? Is it happening across model sizes or just the large ones?

ken: Trace excerpt they sent: 
```
span: token_emit 920ms p99
span: model_forward 38ms
span: gpu_wait 855ms (stall)
kv_cache_miss: 12%
node: eu2-gpu-12
```

anita: Any infra changes in eu2 around that window? We did a rolling host/kernel/driver push last week.

ken: Deploy logs show a CUDA driver update (520.56.1) rolled through eu2 Thu 21:30-22:15 and we pushed GPU firmware microcode v2.14 with the AMI rebuild at ~21:40.

sarah: Hmm — could be firmware-induced PCIe resyncs or a power/thermal governor change. Do we see PCIe/PCIEe link events or increased nvlink retries?

ken: Customer syslog shows these lines around the spike:
```
[21:44:51] nvidia-microcode: updated to v2.14
[21:45:03] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Corrected error, device resumed
[21:45:03] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected
```

ops-bot: alert: node eu2-gpu-12 pcie_err_count increased x3 at 2024-11-14T21:45:03Z :rotating_light:

mike: Repro plan: run a synthetic multi-client stream to try to trigger tail stalls. Script: 4 concurrent clients, each streaming tokens to saturate KV hits+misses for 3-5m. If it's firmware/PCIe, repro may be intermittent. Also collect `nvidia-smi dmon -s u`, `dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200`, `sudo perf record -a -g -F 99 -- sleep 300`.

anita: I'll spin a canary in eu2 with the same AMI (driver+fw v2.14) and run the bench. Enabling pcie and nvme counters: `sudo modprobe pcieport_hotplug` + `ethtool -S` on the host NICs, and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=pcie.link_utilization --format=csv`.

ken: Customer notes it only hit nodes in one physical rack. Could be a noisy PSU or PCIe lane flapping rather than model code.

sarah: Another quick mitigation: pin the customer to an isolated node pool (eu2-isolated-1) and steer traffic away from nodes with pcie_err_count > 0. Also add a temporary fallback routing rule to serve a smaller model variant for tail-sensitive requests. That should buy time without a heavy rollback. :white_check_mark:

anita: I'm launching the canary now and will enable kernel tracepoints for nv_pcie_error and nvme. Command I run:
```
sudo perf record -e pci:* -a sleep 120
sudo trace-cmd record -e nv_pcie_error -e nvme:completion -o /tmp/trace.dat -- sleep 120
```

mike: If the canary reproduces, next step is to isolate whether the driver or the firmware microcode is the root cause. Prefer to validate PCIe error correlation first, then test a driver rollback on a single canary node (keep firmware the same) to see if behavior changes.

ken: Customer agreed to pin + fallback while we triage. They want an ETA on root cause.

sarah: I'll create a monitor/alert for pcie_err_count and add a temporary SLO relaxation. Also adding a tracing hook in the request path to capture kernel dmesg snippets on first token stall.

ops-bot: action: created incidents/1234 (isolate node group), incidents/1235 (canary driver rollback), incidents/1236 (collect perf/trace artifacts).

ken: Thanks — I'll loop the customer with these mitigations and ask them to keep traffic steady while we run the synthetic load. Will post canary results here. :pray:
